conversation.content:
Hi there—my name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived, not to judge or label you in any way. We’ll use a short questionnaire called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. It’s just 10 questions about the past week, and it helps us spot moms who might be struggling with postpartum depression or anxiety so we can offer the right support. Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger. We’ll go at your pace, and you can pause any time. Ready to begin?

In the past seven days, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly... not very often. I’ll catch myself smiling at the baby every now and then, but actually laughing—like really laughing—feels kind of foreign lately. Most of the time I’m too tired or worried about something going wrong.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I guess I’d say “not so much now.” I can still chuckle once in a while if something’s really silly, but it’s nowhere near as easy or natural as it used to be. Most days I just feel too worn-out or on-edge to find the humor in things.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. Even stuff I used to get excited about—like meeting a friend for coffee or going for a walk—just feels like another chore. I’ll think, “That might be nice,” but then I’m too tired or I worry the baby will fuss the whole time, so I don’t bother.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that a lot. If the baby cries longer than usual, I immediately think it’s because I’m not doing something right—like I missed his cue or I’m not comforting him the way he needs. Even little things, like spilling a bottle or taking too long to soothe him, turn into this loop of “I’m failing at being his mom.” I know rationally it’s not all on me, but in the moment it feels like every hiccup is my fault.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Pretty much every day. I’ll be feeding her and suddenly my heart’s racing because I’m sure she’s not breathing right, or I’ll lie down at night and my mind keeps spinning with all these “what-ifs”—fever, choking, SIDS, anything. Nothing’s actually wrong, but I can’t shake the feeling that something bad is about to happen.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah… I get that sudden rush of fear out of nowhere—like my chest tightens and I feel shaky. It’s happened a few times this week, usually when the baby’s asleep and the house is quiet. There’s no real reason for it, but in the moment I feel like something awful is about to happen and I can’t calm myself down for a while.
Things have been getting on top of me

Most days, honestly. It feels like the second I finish one thing—feeding, changing, trying to get her to nap—there’s already another bottle to wash or a pile of laundry that’s been sitting there for days. I’ll look around the apartment and just feel… buried. I keep telling myself, “Take it step by step,” but by late afternoon I’m snapping at my partner over nothing and then feeling guilty about that, too. I’m not falling apart completely, but yeah, it’s like I’m always one tiny setback away from tears.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes… I lie down exhausted, but my head won’t settle. I keep replaying every little thing I might’ve done wrong—did I burp her long enough, did I miss a dirty diaper, am I already ruining her? I’ll finally drift off, then any tiny grunt from the bassinet jolts me awake and the worrying starts all over. I’m lucky if I get three broken hours a night.
I have felt sad or miserable

That’s most of the day, every day. I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling that just sits on me. I’ll look at the baby and feel love, but it’s like there’s a thick window between us—I can see how precious she is, yet the joy feels muffled. Some afternoons I just sit on the couch nursing her with tears slipping down for no clear reason except everything feels hopeless and I can’t shake it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah… it’s happened a few times this week. The littlest thing sets me off—like when I spilled the pumped milk yesterday and just sat on the kitchen floor sobbing because it felt like I’d wasted the only thing I’m actually good at giving her right now. Most nights, once my partner’s asleep, the tears just come and I can’t stop them even when I tell myself I should be grateful.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No… I haven’t thought about hurting myself. I feel lousy and overwhelmed, but I’d never want to leave my baby without a mom. I just want to feel better, not gone.

stats.query:
postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 24: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: 10-item Edinburgh-based interview, 0–3 self-ratings inferred from narrative.

Areas endorsed (approx. score ≥2):
- Laughing/pleasure markedly ↓ (Q1≈2, Q2≈2)
- Persistent self-blame, guilt (Q3≈2)
- Daily free-floating anxiety & panic symptoms (Q4≈2, Q5≈2)
- Overwhelm, coping fatigue (Q6≈2)
- Sleep initiation/maintenance impaired by intrusive worry (Q7≈2)
- Pervasive sadness, tearfulness (Q8≈2, Q9≈2)

Key patterns:
- Consenting low mood with anhedonia, guilt cognitions, and physiologic anxiety.
- Sleep disruption tied to ruminative worry, not solely infant demands.
- No self-harm ideation reported (Q10≈0).

Screening significance:
Findings exceed “baby blues” threshold; meet provisional criteria for moderate–severe postpartum depression with comorbid anxiety. Safety: no suicidal intent voiced; will continue to monitor.

Next steps (per protocol):
- Discuss results; offer formal EPDS questionnaire and referral to OB mental-health team.
- Provide psycho-education, support resources, crisis line numbers.
- Schedule follow-up within 1 week to reassess mood, anxiety, sleep, and parenting stress.
